items.title: aiohttp server lacks an initial request/header timeout
items.summary: Summary The keepalive timeout was not used during the initial portion of a request. Impact An attacker could keep an idle connection open indefinitely before sending any data. Workaround Use a reverse proxy (as recommended for all production deployments) with sensible keepalive limits.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Secure attribute not enforced for shared cookie
items.summary: Summary The Secure attribute was not being enforced for the shared cookie. Impact It may be possible to send a shared cookie marked Secure through an unencrypted request.

items.title: aiohttp: Multiple instances of excessive or unbounded memory/CPU use
items.summary: Summary Multiple cases were found where aiohttp could use excessive or unbounded memory, or excessive CPU consumption on attacker controlled requests. Impact An attacker could cause resource exhaustion through specially crafted requests.

items.title: Mercury: Stored / DOM Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): mr.Markdown renders untrusted content as raw, unsanitized HTML
items.summary: Summary Mercury turns Jupyter notebooks into shared web apps/dashboards. The mr.Markdown widget converts its input to HTML with python-markdown and no sanitization step . MarkdownWidget is an ipywidgets.HTML widget, whose value is written to the page as raw HTML (via innerHTML ) with no sanitization , so the result reaches the DOM verbatim. When an app passes untrusted data (database rows, user submissions, uploaded file contents, or an external/LLM API response) to mr.Markdown , HTML/JS in that data executes in the browser of whoever views the app — a d

items.summary: Summary A missing comma in mercury app/block handler.py 's BLOCKED PATTERNS list causes the blocklist to fail to cover the /api/terminals endpoint. items.title: Graphify Fortran extractor: incomplete cpp include hardening allows arbitrary host-file read/exfiltration when indexing an untrusted repo
items.summary: Summary The Fortran extractor's C-preprocessor step ( graphify/extractors/fortran.py , cpp preprocess ) applies an incomplete include hardening. The -nostdinc -I /dev/null flags it relies on (comment "Security (F-007)") do not stop a capital- F Fortran source file from including absolute paths ( include "/etc/passwd" ) or from path-traversing out of the corpus ( include "../../../../home/victim/.ssh/id rsa" ). cpp always searches the directory of the file being preprocessed for quoted includes and always honours absolute include paths, regardless of -nos

items.title: Mercury: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via /api/kernels
items.summary: Mercury runs a JupyterLab server with anonymous access by default ( mercury app/ main .py sets --IdentityProvider.token='' when no --token / MERCURY TOKEN is given; when tokenless it also sets --ServerApp.disable check xsrf=True ). It relies on a blocklist ( mercury app/block handler.py BLOCKED PATTERNS : /lab , /api/terminals , /api/shutdown , /files ) to keep anonymous users off dangerous Jupyter endpoints. items.title: LoopX serve-status permissive CORS policy exposes control-plane state and private Markdown files
items.summary: Summary loopx serve-status sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: on every response, including its unauthenticated GET routes. Because the endpoint is unauthenticated and bound to a fixed, well-known loopback port, any website the operator visits can read LoopX control-plane state and the contents of Markdown files inside every registered goal repo , using a plain fetch() with no user interaction. The write endpoints are not affected — they are correctly Origin-checked. This report is strictly about the read paths. Impact While loopx serve-status is running,

The intended clients are sibling LMCache processes. There is no CURVE, ZAP, password, or message authentication on that socket. LMCache used only inside a vLLM process does not open this port. items.title: Claude Agent SDK: Argument Injection via resume Option Allows Arbitrary Command Execution
items.summary: The Claude Agent SDK for Python passed the resume option to the Claude CLI without validation, allowing a value beginning with - to be interpreted as a separate CLI flag. An attacker who controlled the resume value could inject an --mcp-config flag defining a stdio MCP server, resulting in arbitrary command execution at CLI startup that bypassed the SDK's permission controls. Exploitation required an application to pass untrusted input as the session ID to resume. Users are advised to update to the latest version of the claude-agent-sdk package. Thank yo

items.title: ClickMigrate has Path Traversal in "revision -m" argument
items.summary: Impact A path traversal vulnerability in the revision command allowed a crafted migration name supplied via the -m argument to escape the intended migrations directory. Under specific conditions, an attacker could cause the tool to create a .sql file in an arbitrary location writable by the user executing the command. This issue is only exploitable if an attacker can influence the migration name passed to the revision command, such as through an insecure automation or CI/CD pipeline that forwards untrusted input. Patches The vulnerability has been fixed

items.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Authentication Bypass by Spoofing Vulnerability
items.summary: Known exploited vulnerability catalog addition: BeyondTrust Remote Support contains an authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to perform file operations on the appliance.

items.title: Fortinet Multiple Products Path Traversal Vulnerability
items.summary: Known exploited vulnerability catalog addition: FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager contain a path traversal vulnerability that may allow an authenticated attacker with admin profile and at least read-write permissions to write or delete arbitrary files via specific CLI commands.

items.title: Pipecat: Public exposure of Pipecat’s development runner can allow unauthenticated bot session creation
items.summary: Pipecat’s built-in development runner exposes endpoints that create bot sessions and, for the Daily transport, paid Daily rooms. These development endpoints intentionally do not authenticate callers. The runner binds to localhost by default and is designed exclusively for local development. It is not built or supported as a production server. items.title: JupyterLab: Command link trust prompt in JupyterLab can trust a document other than the one clicked
items.summary: Description A Markdown file or a notebook output can carry a button that runs a JupyterLab command. Since 4.5.7 the first click on such a button opens a prompt naming the command, with Cancel, Run Once and Trust. Choosing Trust runs the command and marks the document trusted, so its later buttons run without a prompt. Which document gets marked is decided when the user answers, not when they click. items.title: tinytag: Infinite loop when parsing certain M4A files containing invalid atoms
items.summary: Impact An M4A file containing a sub-atom with a size of zero in the ---- atom makes the parser enter an infinite loop, resulting in a denial-of-service for programs reading such files with tinytag. Patches The issue has been fixed in tinytag 2.3.0, by reusing the primary atom parsing code path that contains appropriate size checks. Workarounds No workarounds exist. Users must upgrade to tinytag 2.3.0.

items.title: copyparty FTP: upload outside defined volumes (limited path traversal)
items.summary: The FTP and FTPS server -- if enabled -- would allow uploading to any folder that the copyparty process had permission to write to. The FTP-server is default-disabled, and must be explicitly enabled in the config with global-option ftp or ftps to be affected. Additionally, SFTP was not affected at all; only FTP and FTPS. This was not a full read/write path-traversal; it had the following limitations: Only applied to uploads; it was not possible to read/download existing files in this manner. Each session also kept its parsed initialize parameters, and the number of sessions was unlimited. items.title: borg extract might modify out-of-tree files when extracting maliciously crafted archives
items.summary: Impact A maliciously crafted archive could contain a symlink (e.g. "evil" - "/etc") followed by an item below it ("evil/passwd"), or an item whose path embeds ".." (e.g. "a/../../etc/passwd"). When extracting such items, borg followed the symlink / resolved the "..", so it could delete or overwrite files outside the extraction directory. In a quite similar scenario, a crafted archive could contain a slave hardlink item with the hardlink source pointing outside the extraction directory. items.title: Python Social Auth: Login CSRF in LINE backend (LineOAuth2) — missing OAuth state validation (incomplete fix of 5.0.0 campaign)
items.summary: Impact Applications using the LINE Login backend are vulnerable to login CSRF / forced authentication. An attacker can start a LINE authorization flow for an account they control and trick a victim into visiting the callback URL with the attacker’s authorization code. Because the LINE backend did not validate the returned OAuth state, the application could accept the forged callback and log the victim in as the attacker-controlled LINE account. items.title: Atlassian Multiple Products Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties Vulnerability
items.summary: Known exploited vulnerability catalog addition: Multiple Atlassian products (Bitbucket Data Center ,Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center, Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye) contain a files or directories accessible to external parties vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions.

items.title: BBOT's Symlink guard bypass in unarchive module allows planting symlinks during extraction
items.summary: BBOT's unarchive module rejects archives containing symlink entries before extraction, but for zip and 7z archives it failed to detect symlinks whose listing carries a DOS-attribute prefix before the unix mode, as produced by legacy versions of p7zip. Such an archive, downloaded and extracted during a scan (for example via filedownload ), bypassed the guard and caused an attacker-controlled symlink to be written into the extraction directory. items.title: Apprise forwards configured auth headers across cross-origin HTTP redirects
items.summary: Summary Apprise's HTTP-based notification plugins and its HTTP attachment / config loaders ( apprise/attachment/http.py , apprise/config/http.py ) follow HTTP 3xx redirects by default and re-send the user-configured auth headers and query parameters on the redirected request . items.title: Ahsay AhsayCBS Command Injection Vulnerability
items.summary: Known exploited vulnerability catalog addition: Ahsay AhsayCBS contains a command injection vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute operating system commands via manipulation of the random parameter in the Replication Receiver component’s /rps/api/json/UpdateReceivers.do endpoint. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-105133.

items.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Relative Path Traversal Vulnerability

items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Authentication Bypass by Spoofing Vulnerability

items.summary: Known exploited vulnerability catalog addition: Microsoft Windows Shell contains a command injection vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

items.title: Shiny for Python has path traversal in bookmark restore
items.summary: Impact Shiny for Python's bookmark-restore path accepted a client-supplied state id query-string value and joined it into the server-side bookmark directory ( /shiny bookmarks/ ) without validating it. A value containing .. path segments, or an absolute path, could therefore cause the server to open and parse input.json and values.json from a directory outside the bookmark store. items.title: pacioli: A submit consent marker licensed cancellation of caller-named pre-existing documents
items.summary: Impact pacioli-guard 's document-layer consent gate requires a human-minted, single-use, document-bound and act-bound marker before a credential carrying API Key Scope.require consent may submit or cancel a document. Because ERPNext performs further document writes as a consequence of a governed act, nested acts are allowed to "ride" the consent established by the enclosing act instead of needing a marker of their own. The ride predicate returned true for every cancel, regardless of which act the enclosing marker authorised. Riding never reaches consent

items.title: pyload-ng: getUserData/get userdata exposed at Perms.ANY allow any authenticated account to brute-force the administrator password
items.summary: Summary Api.getUserData (legacy) and Api.get userdata are declared with @permission(Perms.ANY) and are reachable at /api/getUserData and /api/get userdata . Because Perms.ANY == 0 and pyLoad's permission check is a bitmask AND, that gate is a no-op: every authenticated account passes, including one holding zero permission bits. Both methods are thin wrappers around check auth() , which the maintainers deliberately restricted to administrators by omitting @permission (no entry in perm map , so is authorized() returns False for non-admins). items.title: pyLoad: Rate-Limit Bypass and Audit-Log Spoofing via Trusted Client-Controlled X-Forwarded-For Header
items.summary: Summary pyLoad determines the "client IP" used for its rate-limiting decorator and for its security/audit logging by reading the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For (XFF) HTTP header and taking the leftmost value. No trusted-proxy configuration exists (the Cheroot WSGI server faces clients directly, and there is no ProxyFix middleware). items.title: pyLoad: Privilege revocation and password change through the REST API do not invalidate the user's session
items.summary: An admin who revokes a user's privileges through the REST API does not actually revoke them, because the session carrying those privileges is never invalidated. pyLoad authorizes each request from values copied into the Flask session at login. set session in webui/app/helpers.py writes role and perms once, and both login required and the session branch of apikey auth read them back from the session rather than from the database. items.title: pyLoad: Api.set user permission never invalidates the target's session
